assessmentSummary.identity: Consecutive forward bounds with one-foot takeoff and landing on alternating legs, coordinated contralateral arm action, the exact projection/contact-time intent named by the variant, and a controlled run-out.
currentCardFindings: Alternate-Leg Bound for Distance, Alternate Bounds for Height and Distance, generic Alternating Bounds, and Alternating Bounds for Height share the same alternating unilateral base action.
The four legacy definitions incompletely express projection, contact-time intent, start leg, distance or contacts, effort, finish, run-out, dose, quality gates, and stop rules.
Legacy prose using level-4 describes an impact tier but is ambiguous with athlete proficiency; the canonical card uses explicit high repeated unilateral impact instead.

Three inherited links identify lateral-bound or scissor-jump exercises, and five more inherited links identify same-leg bounds. All eight remain traceable mismatches rather than candidate demonstrations.
Five newly discovered links returned current title, channel, and oEmbed metadata but still require full human exact-variant, instruction, safety, caption, accessibility, and approval review.

proposedDosage.technique: 2-4 sets of 4-8 contacts or 8-15 meters at 60-85% intent with 60-150 seconds recovery
proposedDosage.output: 2-4 sets of 6-12 contacts or 15-30 meters at 85-100% intent with 120-240 seconds recovery
proposedDosage.progressWhen: every sequence preserves alternation, active non-reaching contact, variant-matched projection, posture, arms, symmetry, rhythm, and controlled run-out

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Retain one stable Alternating Bounds identity with traditional mixed height-distance and sprint distance/rhythm variants. Keep the card in review until evidence, media, graph, calibration, pilot, and publication gates receive real human decisions.

currentCardSnapshot.description: From a declared start, perform consecutive forward bounds with one-foot takeoff and landing on alternating legs, coordinated contralateral arm action, and the exact projection and contact-time intent named by the variant. Preserve posture, active contacts under the body, side-to-side rhythm, and a controlled run-out; stop before reaching, collapse, asymmetry, contact noise, or output loss.

population.medicalScope: This card is not rehabilitation, tendon treatment, diagnosis, or clearance; follow the athlete care plan and local scope.

evidence.sourceTitle: Plyometric Training Practices of Brazilian Olympic Sprint and Jump Coaches: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Their Choices and Insights
claims: Alternating Bounds uses consecutive unilateral forward contacts with alternating legs and coordinated running-style arm action.

Traditional mixed-projection and sprint-oriented distance forms are exact variants; projection emphasis, contact-time intent, distance, contacts, effort, and measurement do not create athlete proficiency categories.

evidence.sourceTitle: Relationship and Training Effects of Horizontal Multi-Step Jumps on Sprint Performance: A Systematic Review
claims: The family is a rectilinear horizontal multi-step plyometric with alternating unilateral contacts.
Same-leg hops, straight-leg bounds, skips, lateral bounds, obstacles, and bounds linked to a sprint change contact sequence, joint strategy, direction, constraint, or terminal action.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of Plyometric Training on Lower Body Muscle Architecture, Tendon Structure, Stiffness and Physical Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
claims: Repeated bounding contacts load the lower-limb muscle-tendon system, including plantarflexors and Achilles exposure, knee and hip extensors, foot structures, and trunk stabilization.
Contralateral arm action contributes to whole-body coordination; the card does not claim isolated-muscle outcomes.

evidence.sourceTitle: Plyometric Training Practices of Brazilian Olympic Sprint and Jump Coaches: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Their Choices and Insights
claims: Traditional and sprint alternate bounds retain the same alternating base action but differ in contact-time intent, landing strategy, and projection.
The card does not impose a universal contact-time target and rejects reaching, collapse, asymmetry, or fatigue-driven strategy change.

evidence.sourceTitle: Relationship and Training Effects of Horizontal Multi-Step Jumps on Sprint Performance: A Systematic Review
claims: Bounding combines multi-step projection, unilateral landings, rhythm, and whole-body coordination under time and distance constraints.
Each exact variant is scored only for exercise complexity and physical difficulty, with overall equal to their maximum; athlete readiness and experience remain workout-selection inputs.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of Plyometric Training on Lower Body Muscle Architecture, Tendon Structure, Stiffness and Physical Performance: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
claims: Track actual unilateral contacts, distance, intensity, surface, calf-Achilles, hamstring, quadriceps and gluteal fatigue, eccentric stress, asymmetry, and recovery.
Stop before contact, projection, posture, rhythm, symmetry, or run-out quality declines.
Require an appropriate surface, straight separated lane, clear run-out, progressive exposure, and direct observation.
Readiness and environment determine whether to use the card; the exercise itself has no skill-library level.

evidence.sourceTitle: Maximizing plyometric training for adolescents: a meta-analysis of ground contact frequency and overall intervention time on jumping ability
evidence.sourcePublisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
claims: Ground contacts and total exposure are material plyometric dose variables.
Use conservative contact and distance ranges with adequate recovery, and record actual rather than planned contacts.

evidence.sourceTitle: Plyometric Training Practices of Brazilian Olympic Sprint and Jump Coaches: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Their Choices and Insights
claims: Declare traditional or sprint form, start leg, distance or contacts, effort, finish, run-out, rest, and stop signal.
Visible execution gates are correct alternation, active non-reaching contact, variant-matched projection, organized hips and trunk, contralateral arms, side-to-side rhythm, and controlled run-out.
Stop for pain, pulling, giving way, unsafe surface or traffic, reaching, loud or collapsing contact, alternation error, meaningful asymmetry, output loss, or uncontrolled run-out.
Reduce intensity, contacts, and distance before increasing form or speed demands.

evidence.sourceTitle: Effects of Vertically and Horizontally Orientated Plyometric Training on Physical Performance: A Meta-analytical Comparison
claims: Horizontal plyometric orientation is relevant to horizontal performance, but card choice still depends on the exact session objective and cumulative load.
Place high-intent bounds while fresh and count them against unilateral jump, sprint, impact, calf-Achilles, hamstring, eccentric, and technical budgets.
Athletes receive exact setup, contact, dose, finish, self-check, symptom, and stop guidance before the first sequence.
Written, still-image, walkthrough, and live-demonstration alternatives remain available.

evidence.sourceTitle: Plyometric Training Practices of Brazilian Olympic Sprint and Jump Coaches: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Their Choices and Insights
claims: The coach distinguishes traditional from sprint form and observes projection, foot placement, contact intent, posture, arms, symmetry, rhythm, fatigue, and finish.
Actual contacts, distance, stopped attempts, faults, and symptoms remain traceable.

evidence.sourceTitle: Maximizing plyometric training for adolescents: a meta-analysis of ground contact frequency and overall intervention time on jumping ability
evidence.sourcePublisher: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
claims: Intensity, distance, contacts, form, recovery, instruction format, and supervision can be individualized without classifying the exercise by athlete level.
When the alternating contact pattern cannot be controlled, use a reviewed regression instead of changing the identity definition.

evidence.sourceTitle: Relationship and Training Effects of Horizontal Multi-Step Jumps on Sprint Performance: A Systematic Review
claims: Traditional mixed-projection and sprint-oriented distance forms are variants of alternating bounds.
Same-leg, straight-leg, skip, lateral, obstacle, resisted, and bound-to-sprint executions require separate identity or variant review according to their changed mechanics.
YouTube supports privacy-enhanced embedding through youtube-nocookie.com.

Five title-matched candidates returned current oEmbed metadata; eight inherited lateral, scissor-jump, or same-leg titles are quarantined mismatches. No playback, exact-match, caption, accessibility, reviewer, or approval claim is made.

alternateAssessments.name: Alternate Bounds for Height and Distance
alternateAssessments.rationale: The source retains alternating unilateral forward contacts; mixed projection is the traditional exact variant.

alternateAssessments.name: Alternate-Leg Bound for Distance
alternateAssessments.rationale: The stable source retains alternating unilateral forward contacts; sprint-distance emphasis is an exact variant.

alternateAssessments.name: Traditional Alternating Bound
alternateAssessments.rationale: Longer powerful contacts with mixed vertical-horizontal projection preserve the alternating base action.

alternateAssessments.name: Sprint Alternating Bound
alternateAssessments.rationale: Shorter active contacts and faster horizontal rhythm preserve the alternating base action.

alternateAssessments.name: Same-Leg Bounds
alternateAssessments.rationale: Repeated takeoff and landing on the same leg changes contact sequence, unilateral accumulation, rhythm, and side dosing.

alternateAssessments.name: Straight-Leg Bounds
alternateAssessments.rationale: A deliberately stiff-knee cyclic action changes joint strategy and intent.

alternateAssessments.name: Power Skip for Height
alternateAssessments.rationale: A step-hop skip cycle and vertical emphasis differ from bound-to-opposite-leg contacts.

alternateAssessments.name: Power Skip for Distance
alternateAssessments.rationale: A step-hop skip cycle differs from consecutive opposite-leg bounds.

alternateAssessments.name: Lateral Alternating Bound
alternateAssessments.rationale: Frontal-plane projection changes direction, landing strategy, space, and coaching.

alternateAssessments.name: Hurdle Alternating Bounds
alternateAssessments.rationale: An obstacle fixes flight and clearance constraints and changes failure consequence and equipment.

alternateAssessments.name: Resisted Alternating Bounds
alternateAssessments.rationale: A declared light resistance may preserve the alternating action but materially changes external load and contact timing and requires exact review.

alternateAssessments.name: Straight-Leg Bounds to Sprint
alternateAssessments.rationale: A prescribed transition into sprinting adds an ordered action and acceleration dose.
